messages:
talia: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change yesterday we started seeing a small but consistent tail regression in eu-west when requests spill to other zones. TL;DR: p95 up ~40ms on cross-zone spill events.

kevin: Thanks for flagging. Is this only when spillover actually moves a batch, or also when we attempt and fail?

talia: Looks like when we move batches (spill succeeded). Local queues are fine. When remote kernel is selected we see higher per-token latency and KV cache miss rate spikes.

anika: Do we have profiler traces for an affected request? can we correlate with kernel path / quantized codegen?

talia: I grabbed a trace and a small perf diff. Paste below. The hot path is in kernel_dispatch -> kv_restore where we wait on remote RPC + deserializing big KV pages.

talia: ```
# simplified stack from perf flame:
kernel_dispatch()
  -> select_kernel_variant()  // picks avx vs cuda fallback
  -> continuous_batcher::form_batch()
  -> kv_restore()  // remote fetch path
  -> json::deserialize (40ms)
  -> emit_tokens()

note: remote fetch adds ~25-35ms, deserialization ~10-15ms
```

jorge: Hmm — that json::deserialize jump smells like we restructured the KV wire format after the selector change. Are we falling back to the legacy compact encoding for cross-zone deserial?

kevin: We did add a compatibility path for older kernels. If the chosen kernel tag != local canonical, we do a decode-to-canonical then re-encode for the target variant. That could explain extra copies.

elaine: Oncall saw a spike at 03:12 UTC, I linked the saga to the rollout. Can we put a temporary affinity override to prefer local variant unless queue depth > X?

talia: Proposed emergency tweak: raise local_affinity_threshold to 0.85 and set cross_zone_spill_token_budget to 6 tokens (was 12). The idea: avoid spilling small batches that pay high RPC/deserialize cost.

anika: I like the token budget change. Small batches are disproportionately expensive when KV miss + RPC. We should also consider coalescing KV requests across spilled batches (batch-level prefetch).

kevin: Agree on both. Quick patch to kernel selector to prefer local variant when estimated spill cost > estimated kernel perf delta. Pseudocode:

kevin: ```
spill_cost = rpc_latency_est + kv_deser_cost - local_cache_hit_saving
kernel_gain = remote_kernel_expected_throughput - local_kernel_throughput
if kernel_gain < spill_cost: prefer_local_variant()
else: allow_spill()
```

talia: Can we get telemetry for rpc_latency_est per zone and per model? Need basis for thresholds.

jorge: I'll add a short metric: runtime.crosszone.rpc_latency_p50/p95 per model+zone and runtime.kv.deserialize_ms. Should be available in ~30m.

perf-bot: regression-alert: eu-west p95 token-latency +42ms vs baseline for model:gpt-native-v2 during 03:00-04:00 UTC.

elaine: Until we have a proper tune, please roll back the kernel selector change in eu-west canary. I'll set the restart and pin to previous kernel tag.

kevin: Rolling back canary now. Also starting an experiment branch with the kernel_gain vs spill_cost heuristic (will push PR: infra/selector: multi-cluster spill heur).

anika: For the longer term: 1) cache-compatible wire format (zero-copy) 2) predictive batching that prefers forming slightly larger local batches to amortize KV fetch 3) cross-zone coalesced KV fetch.

talia: Agree. Added a TODO in the runtime board: link: https://redwood/internal/boards/runtime/tickets/3221. Also saved the profiler snapshot to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1934567890-euw-spill-1.trace

jorge: FYI, infra will also add a small egress QoS bump for kernel RPCs between eu zones for 24h to reduce variance while we tune.

talia: Thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) rollback done (elaine) (2) metrics added (jorge) (3) selector heuristic PR (kevin) (4) perf diff + wire-format investigation (anika). I'll update thread when we have first numbers. :thumbsup:

elaine: Great coordination. If we still see p95 > +25ms after heuristic, I'll open an incident.

kevin: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/selector/pulls/128 — implements spill_cost heuristic + config flags. Please review.

talia: Reviewing now. Quick ask: please expose the two knobs as runtime flags so we can tweak in prod without full rollout.

kevin: Will do. ETA for review + merge ~2h.

anika: I'll start a small microbench to measure deserialize cost per serialization version and push results to the ticket.

perf-bot: perf-check: deserial-v2 median 9ms, deserial-v1 median 22ms (same payload) — details in perf dashboard.

talia: Excellent — that explains most of it. Thank you.

kevin: Thanks team. Plan: monitor after rollback and then iterate on heuristic + wire-format.
